title: Why 90°? 2D Collisions Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Pool balls split apart at an angle. Two players collide and both are knocked sideways. And when Aarav hits a carrom coin a little off centre, the two fly apart at an angle. With two equal coins, the split always seems to be a right angle. Why 90 degrees, every time? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn collisions in two dimensions.

On a live motion notebook two equal coins collide off centre, seen from above, while the readout tracks the x and y momentum and the split angle, and a graph shows the y momentum of each coin cancelling to zero. A slow-mo replay freezes the touch: the push acts along the line of centres. We check momentum along x and along y with real numbers, prove step by step why equal masses in an elastic hit split at 90 degrees, see link by link why a heavier carrom striker splits at less than 90, compare equal and unequal masses side by side, and solve two bodies that stick at an angle. Then the exam trap (the 90 degree rule needs three conditions), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
